passage:
A baker worked with historians to recreate bread from an old recipe. The grain was rough, and the bread was heavier than modern bread.
Students tasted it during a museum visit. Some liked it. Others found it too dense.
The guide explained that food texture changes with tools, ovens, crops, and taste preferences.
The bread made the past physical. Students were not only hearing about history. They were chewing it.
The experience showed that progress is not always simple. Modern bread may be softer, but old bread reflected different conditions and skills.
Food history teaches through the mouth as well as the mind.
